items.prompt: White to move. White starts the captures on d5 with the pawn: exd5. Black recaptures whenever it can, and White recaptures in turn. Is White ahead when the captures stop? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Two White pieces attack d5: the pawn and the rook.
One Black piece defends d5: the pawn on c6.
Starting with the pawn, White comes out at least 3 points ahead along the best defence.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d5 first. Then ask which capture comes first.
Play the captures out in order. After each one, add what White has won and what White has lost.
Add up the whole sequence: what does White take, and what does White give up?
items.explain: The pawn goes first: it takes the bishop, the pawn on c6 takes back, and the rook takes that pawn. White gives a pawn and wins a bishop and a pawn.

items.prompt: Same position. This time White starts with the rook: Rxd5. Black recaptures whenever it can, and White recaptures in turn. Is White ahead when the captures stop? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Two White pieces attack d5: the pawn and the rook.
One Black piece defends d5: the pawn on c6.
Starting with the rook, White ends at least 1 point behind along the best defence.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d5 first. Then ask which capture comes first.

items.explain: Rxd5 cxd5 exd5: the rook is given for a bishop and a pawn, which is a counting loss. The count (two against one) was the same; the order of the captures made the difference.

feedback_by_move.d1d5: Rxd5 cxd5 exd5 costs a rook for a bishop and a pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. How many of White's pieces are loose (attacked and not defended; kings do not count)? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The only loose White piece is the bishop on d4.

hints: Go through White's pieces one at a time. For each, ask: is it attacked? If so, can a White piece take back on that square?

A piece counts as loose only if it is attacked and nothing of its own side defends it. Kings do not count.
items.explain: The knight on c6 attacks the bishop on d4 and no White piece defends it, so exactly one White piece is loose.

items.prompt: Find the best move.

claims.statement: The queen on g4 is the only loose White piece.
Qxg6 is the engine's best move.
Ignoring the threat with a3 is far worse.

items.explain: The black queen attacks the loose queen on g4. Qxg6 takes the attacker, and the pawn on f7 takes back; the engine rates a quiet move such as a3 far worse because Black then wins the queen.
